catalogue: Australian residential cold-formed steel framing physical objects

ncc_references.relationship: Primary Deemed-to-Satisfy pathway context for residential and low-rise steel framing.

objects.name: cold-formed steel framing system
objects.definition: A coordinated building frame made mainly from thin metallic-coated steel sheet formed into structural sections and assembled as wall, floor and roof frames with compatible bracing and connections.
functions: Carry building loads through light-gauge steel members
Provide wall, floor and roof framing geometry
Coordinate proprietary member capacities, connections, bracing and durability

cad.pattern: Coordinated prefabricated or site-assembled wall, floor and roof frames
cad.placement: Throughout the building structural envelope and internal support lines
cad.opening: Members and connections are scheduled around all openings and service routes
cad.load: Primary light framing system when designed for the project

notes: Member role is stable, but exact section geometry and connection details can be proprietary and must come from the selected frame system.

objects.name: cold-formed steel wall frame
objects.definition: A wall-frame assembly of steel studs between top and bottom tracks or plates, with opening members, noggings, bracing and anchorage as required by the selected system.
functions: Form and support a building wall
Carry vertical and face loads where designed
Provide fixing lines and openings for finishes and services

cad.pattern: Repeated vertical studs captured by continuous top and bottom members
cad.placement: At external and internal wall lines
cad.opening: Stud pattern is replaced by scheduled jamb, lintel and sill framing
cad.load: Loadbearing or non-loadbearing according to frame design

objects.name: loadbearing steel wall frame
objects.definition: A cold-formed steel wall frame designed to carry roof, floor or wall loads in addition to its own weight and face loads.
functions: Carry vertical building loads
Transfer loads to supporting framing or foundations
Provide lateral restraint as part of the designed frame

cad.pattern: Structural wall panels along loadbearing lines
cad.placement: Below supported roof, floor or wall framing
cad.opening: Loads are redirected through jamb posts and lintels

objects.name: non-loadbearing steel wall frame
objects.definition: A cold-formed steel wall frame that supports its own finishes and face loads but is not intended to carry roof or floor gravity loads.
functions: Divide or enclose space
Support linings and claddings
Resist assigned face and service loads without carrying structure above

cad.pattern: Wall panels not aligned to gravity-load supports above
cad.placement: At partition or non-loadbearing enclosure lines
cad.opening: Locally framed for doors and other openings

objects.name: cold-formed steel floor frame
objects.definition: A floor assembly of cold-formed steel bearers, joists, boundary members, blocking and connections that supports flooring and transfers loads to walls, columns or piers.
functions: Support floor decking and imposed loads
Span between bearers or walls
Transfer floor loads to supports

cad.pattern: Repeated joists over bearers or supporting walls
cad.placement: At suspended lower or upper floor levels
cad.opening: Trimmed and connected around floor openings

objects.name: prefabricated steel floor cassette
objects.definition: A transportable prefabricated section of steel floor framing assembled as a panel or ladder-like module before it is installed into the building floor system.
functions: Package joists and boundary members into a liftable module
Accelerate floor-frame installation
Preserve factory set-out and connection locations

cad.pattern: Repeated prefabricated modules joined along planned cassette boundaries
cad.placement: Within a suspended steel floor
cad.opening: Factory-trimmed or site-coordinated openings
cad.load: Modular subassembly of the floor load path

notes: Ladder floor describes one cassette configuration and is not treated as an exact synonym for every prefabricated floor module.

objects.name: cold-formed steel roof frame
objects.definition: A roof-framing assembly made from cold-formed steel rafters, beams or trusses with bracing, battens and connections supporting the roof covering and ceiling.
functions: Support roof and ceiling construction
Transfer roof loads to walls or other supports
Maintain roof geometry and lateral stability

cad.pattern: Repeated trusses or rafters with transverse battens and bracing
cad.placement: Above supporting wall and beam lines
cad.opening: Trusses or rafters are engineered around roof openings

objects.name: cold-formed steel roof truss
objects.definition: An engineered triangulated roof member assembled from cold-formed steel chords and webs connected at nodes and supplied as a complete truss definition.
functions: Span between roof supports
Carry roof and ceiling loads through triangulated members
Provide the roof profile and support for battens

cad.pattern: Repeated engineered trusses at scheduled centres
cad.placement: Across roof-supporting walls or beams
cad.opening: Only fabricator-designed openings and truss modifications

notes: A drawing tool must preserve the fabricator's member and connection layout rather than regenerate it from an outline.

objects.name: steel frame bracing system
objects.definition: The coordinated straps, sheets, members, anchors and hold-downs that stabilise a cold-formed steel wall, floor or roof frame against racking and other lateral movement.
functions: Resist lateral loads
Transfer bracing forces to foundations or supporting structure
Keep frame panels square and stable

cad.pattern: Distributed bracing panels and lines connected to hold-down points
cad.placement: Within wall, floor and roof framing as scheduled
cad.opening: Bracing is placed in clear panels or engineered around openings

notes: One visible strap is not necessarily the complete bracing system.

objects.name: cold-formed steel wall stud
objects.definition: A repeated vertical cold-formed steel member between the top and bottom tracks that supports wall loads, linings and claddings according to its assigned role.
functions: Form the repeated vertical wall frame
Support wall finishes and face loads
Carry vertical loads where selected as a structural stud

cad.pattern: Repeated vertically at system-designed centres
cad.placement: Between wall top and bottom tracks
cad.opening: Replaced or supplemented by opening studs and posts
cad.load: Repeated wall member; capacity depends on section and restraint

objects.name: steel jamb stud
objects.definition: A full-height steel stud or built-up stud group at the side of a wall opening that supports the opening frame and may receive lintel reactions.
functions: Form the side of a wall opening
Support the lintel or beam where designed
Provide fixing for window or door jambs

cad.pattern: One designed stud or stud group at each opening side
cad.placement: Full height beside door and window openings
cad.opening: Defines the opening jamb
cad.load: Opening-side member with possible lintel reaction

objects.name: steel jack stud
objects.definition: A shortened steel stud placed above or below a wall opening where the normal stud pattern cannot continue through the opening.
functions: Continue stud spacing in the short wall zone
Support linings and claddings around an opening
Transfer local load between the opening member and track where designed

cad.pattern: At the normal stud module in wall zones above or below openings
cad.placement: Between lintel and top track or sill and bottom track
cad.opening: Occupies only wall area outside the opening void

notes: Exact proprietary terminology requires confirmation from the selected frame system.

objects.name: built-up steel wall post
objects.definition: A strengthened vertical wall member made from one heavier or several connected cold-formed sections to carry concentrated loads beyond an ordinary repeated stud role.
functions: Carry concentrated vertical loads
Support beam or lintel reactions
Transfer local load through the wall frame

cad.pattern: At concentrated-load and major-opening locations
cad.placement: Within loadbearing wall panels
cad.end: Beam, lintel or truss reaction above
cad.opening: Often placed at opening jambs

objects.name: steel wall top track
objects.definition: The continuous horizontal cold-formed steel track or plate at the top of a wall frame that captures stud ends and distributes or transfers loads and restraint according to the system.
functions: Locate and connect stud tops
Tie the wall panel together
Receive or distribute supported framing loads where designed

cad.pattern: Continuous along wall-panel tops with detailed laps and junctions
cad.placement: Over steel stud ends
cad.opening: Continues over or is detailed around openings according to the frame system

objects.name: steel wall bottom track
objects.definition: The continuous horizontal cold-formed steel track or plate at the base of a wall frame that captures stud ends and connects the wall to its floor or foundation support.
functions: Locate and connect stud bottoms
Tie the wall panel base together
Transfer wall forces to anchors and the supporting construction

cad.pattern: Continuous along wall bases with anchors at scheduled locations
cad.placement: Between studs and supporting slab, floor or frame
cad.opening: Interrupted at door openings where the frame system requires

objects.name: steel wall nogging
objects.definition: A horizontal steel member fixed between wall studs to restrain them, maintain spacing or provide a fixing support for linings, claddings, fixtures or services.
functions: Restrain studs laterally
Maintain stud spacing
Provide intermediate fixing support

cad.pattern: Horizontal rows between studs at system or fixture levels
cad.placement: Between adjacent steel studs
cad.opening: Interrupted and repositioned around openings
cad.load: Stud restraint or local fixing support

objects.name: cold-formed steel wall lintel
objects.definition: A horizontal cold-formed or built-up light-steel member over a wall opening that transfers supported frame, roof or floor loads to the opening-side studs or posts.
functions: Span a framed wall opening
Support framing and loads above
Transfer reactions to jamb studs or posts

cad.pattern: One designed lintel assembly per load-requiring opening
cad.placement: Across the opening head
cad.opening: Spans the clear framed opening
cad.load: Opening beam in the light-steel wall frame

notes: Kept separate from the steel masonry lintel because their hosts, bearings and supported construction differ.

objects.name: steel frame bracing strap
objects.definition: A tension-capable metal strap fixed diagonally across a wall, floor or roof frame as part of a designed bracing system.
functions: Resist racking in tension
Transfer diagonal bracing force to boundary members
Stabilise frame geometry

cad.pattern: Single or opposing diagonal runs across selected frame panels
cad.placement: Fixed to studs and boundary tracks or roof and floor members
cad.opening: Placed in clear bracing panels unless engineered otherwise

objects.name: steel frame bracing sheet
objects.definition: A structural sheet fixed to a steel frame panel with a designed edge and field fixing pattern so the sheet and frame act as a bracing panel.
functions: Resist frame racking through sheet action
Transfer shear to boundary members and hold-downs
Provide a braced wall or floor panel
not_synonyms: ordinary lining without a bracing schedule

cad.pattern: Sheets covering selected complete frame panels
cad.placement: On one or both faces of a braced frame panel
cad.opening: Normally requires specifically designed edges around openings

objects.name: steel frame hold-down bracket
objects.definition: A bracket connecting a bracing-end stud or post to the floor, slab or supporting frame so uplift and overturning forces can pass into the structure below.
functions: Anchor bracing panel ends
Transfer uplift and overturning force
Connect vertical framing to the support below

cad.pattern: At each scheduled bracing-panel end or uplift point
cad.placement: Between boundary stud or post and the support below

objects.name: steel wall-frame anchor
objects.definition: A bolt, screw, nail or proprietary anchor fixing the wall bottom track to a concrete slab, masonry support, timber floor or steel frame at a scheduled location.
functions: Fix the wall frame to its support
Transfer shear, uplift or positioning forces
Maintain wall alignment at the base

cad.pattern: Repeated through bottom track at scheduled centres and bracing points
cad.placement: From bottom track into supporting construction
cad.load: Wall-base fixing; demand varies by location

objects.name: cold-formed steel floor joist
objects.definition: A repeated horizontal cold-formed steel member supporting floor decking and spanning between bearers, walls or other floor supports.
functions: Support floor decking and loads
Span between floor supports
Provide service routes and ceiling fixing support where detailed

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel joists at designed centres
cad.placement: Between floor support lines
cad.opening: Trimmer and connector system replaces normal joists around openings

objects.name: cold-formed steel floor bearer
objects.definition: A primary horizontal cold-formed steel floor member supporting joists and spanning between piers, posts, columns or walls.
functions: Support floor joists
Collect and transfer floor loads
Span between discrete or continuous supports

cad.pattern: Primary support lines beneath repeated joists
cad.placement: On piers, posts, walls or columns
cad.opening: Normally routes beneath rather than around floor openings

notes: Kept separate from Housing Provisions Part 6.3 hot-rolled structural steel bearers.

objects.name: steel floor boundary joist
objects.definition: A cold-formed steel member closing and restraining the edge of a floor frame and providing an attachment line for joist ends, wall frames or edge finishes.
functions: Close the floor-frame perimeter
Restrain joist ends
Provide edge and wall support connections

cad.pattern: Continuous or segmented around the floor perimeter
cad.placement: Across joist ends at floor edges
cad.opening: Forms trimmer boundaries at some edge openings

notes: Preferred system terminology varies between boundary joist, rim joist and rim track.

objects.name: steel floor-joist blocking
objects.definition: A short steel member, strap or proprietary bridging component installed between floor joists to restrain them and distribute lateral movement.
functions: Restrain floor joists against rotation or lateral movement
Maintain joist spacing
Transfer local restraint between adjacent joists

cad.pattern: Rows between joists at designed positions
cad.placement: Between adjacent floor joists
cad.opening: Rows are interrupted and redirected at openings

objects.name: steel floor-joist connector
objects.definition: A proprietary clip, bracket, tab or formed end connection that attaches a cold-formed floor joist to a bearer, boundary member or supporting wall.
functions: Connect a joist end to its support
Transfer bearing, shear and restraint forces
Locate the joist at the correct level and spacing

cad.pattern: One connection at each non-bearing or detailed joist end
cad.placement: Between joist end and bearer, wall or boundary member
cad.opening: Also used at trimming around openings where scheduled

objects.name: cold-formed steel roof rafter
objects.definition: A sloping cold-formed steel roof member supporting battens or roof construction and spanning between the eave support and ridge, beam or other roof support.
functions: Support roof battens and covering
Form the roof slope
Transfer roof loads to walls or beams

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel members down the roof slope
cad.placement: Between eave support and upper roof support
cad.opening: Trimmed or doubled around roof openings only by design

objects.name: cold-formed steel roof beam
objects.definition: A primary cold-formed or built-up light-steel roof member supporting rafters, trusses or concentrated roof loads and spanning between walls or posts.
functions: Support roof-framing reactions
Span between primary supports
Transfer collected roof loads to walls or posts
not_synonyms: Housing Provisions structural steel strutting beam

cad.pattern: At major roof support lines
cad.placement: Below supported rafters or truss reactions
cad.opening: Coordinated around roof openings

objects.name: cold-formed steel roof batten
objects.definition: A light cold-formed steel member fixed across rafters or trusses to support and provide fixing for roof tiles or sheet roofing.
functions: Support roof covering
Provide repeated roof-fixing lines
Restrain rafters or truss top chords where designed

cad.pattern: Repeated transverse runs across roof supports
cad.placement: Over rafters or truss top chords
cad.opening: Trimmed and edge-supported around roof openings

objects.name: cold-formed steel ceiling batten
objects.definition: A light cold-formed steel member fixed beneath trusses, joists or rafters to provide aligned repeated support for ceiling lining.
functions: Support ceiling sheets
Provide a level ceiling fixing plane
Bridge between roof or ceiling framing members

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel runs across ceiling supports
cad.placement: Below truss bottom chords, ceiling joists or rafters
cad.opening: Trimmed around ceiling openings and access hatches
cad.load: Ceiling-lining support only unless otherwise designed

objects.name: steel roof-truss top chord
objects.definition: The sloping upper boundary member of a cold-formed steel roof truss, connected to web members and supporting roof battens or covering loads.
functions: Form the roof slope
Carry roof loads between truss nodes
Connect web forces through the truss

cad.pattern: One or more sloping chord segments per truss
cad.placement: Along the truss roof profile
cad.opening: No unapproved cuts or holes

objects.name: steel roof-truss bottom chord
objects.definition: The lower boundary member of a cold-formed steel roof truss, tying the supports together and commonly providing support for ceiling battens or ceiling loads.
functions: Complete the truss tension or compression chord
Carry ceiling loads where designed
Connect lower web nodes and truss bearings

cad.pattern: Lower chord segments between truss bearings
cad.placement: Along the lower truss profile
cad.opening: No unapproved cuts or holes
cad.load: Engineered truss chord and possible ceiling support

objects.name: steel roof-truss web
objects.definition: An internal diagonal or vertical cold-formed steel member connecting truss chords at nodes and carrying axial force within the triangulated truss.
functions: Transfer force between truss chords
Create the triangulated structural system
Stabilise the chord geometry

cad.pattern: Engineered internal triangulation
cad.placement: Between top and bottom chord nodes
cad.opening: Web layout must not be altered for services

objects.name: steel truss node connection
objects.definition: The screws, rivets, clinches, plates or formed overlaps that physically connect cold-formed steel truss chords and webs at a designed node.
functions: Transfer force between truss members
Hold node geometry
Form part of the engineered truss assembly

cad.pattern: At every chord-to-web and chord splice node
cad.placement: Where truss members meet

notes: The physical form is system-specific; do not assume every steel truss uses a separate gusset plate.

objects.name: steel roof-truss brace
objects.definition: A permanent member or strap connecting multiple steel roof trusses to restrain them and transfer roof-plane or truss-system bracing forces.
functions: Restrain trusses out of plane
Stabilise truss webs or chords
Transfer bracing forces through the roof frame

cad.pattern: Continuous across a group of trusses
cad.placement: At designed chord or web restraint lines
cad.opening: Redirected only by engineered detail
cad.load: Permanent roof and truss stability member

objects.name: cold-formed C-section
objects.definition: A cold-formed steel section with a web and two flanges forming a C-shaped cross-section, used for studs, joists, rafters, bearers or other framing roles.
functions: Provide an efficient light-steel framing cross-section
Form members in several structural roles
Receive connections through web and flanges

cad.pattern: Assigned to members according to the proprietary frame schedule
cad.placement: Any frame role selected for this section
cad.opening: Service holes only as manufactured or approved
cad.load: Cross-section class; structural role comes from the hosted member

notes: A C-section is a shape, not automatically a stud, joist or rafter.

objects.name: cold-formed top-hat section
objects.definition: A cold-formed steel section with a central crown, two webs and outward fixing flanges, commonly used for roof, ceiling or wall battens and some floor members.
functions: Provide a stable fixing face on both sides
Form light spanning or furring members
Allow lapped batten connections where the product permits

cad.pattern: Assigned to compatible batten, joist or furring roles
cad.placement: Across supporting frame members
cad.opening: Trimmed around framed openings
cad.load: Cross-section class; structural role comes from the hosted member

objects.name: steel framing service hole
objects.definition: A factory-punched or approved site-formed opening through a steel framing web that provides a route for electrical wiring, plumbing or other services.
functions: Provide a coordinated route through framing
Reduce unapproved member cutting
Receive a protective grommet where the hole edge could damage or contact the service

cad.pattern: Aligned through compatible member webs where the system provides holes
cad.placement: Near the designed neutral or approved web zone
cad.opening: The object is the physical opening
cad.load: Member opening whose effect must be included in the frame design

notes: A tool must not create extra holes merely because a service route intersects a member.

objects.name: steel framing service-hole grommet
objects.definition: A plastic or other compatible edge fitting snapped into a steel framing service hole to protect cable insulation or isolate piping from the metal edge and frame.
functions: Protect cables from sharp steel edges
Isolate copper pipe from coated steel
Reduce direct service-to-frame contact

cad.pattern: One at each applicable non-flanged occupied service hole
cad.placement: Clipped around the steel hole edge
cad.opening: Lined opening remains clear for the service

objects.name: steel service nogging
objects.definition: A site- or factory-fitted horizontal steel support between studs positioned to carry plumbing fittings, cabinets, equipment or other concentrated wall-mounted items.
functions: Support plumbing and fixture connections
Provide a local screw-fixing rail
Transfer fixture load to adjacent studs

cad.pattern: At scheduled fixture and service outlet locations
cad.placement: Between studs behind the fixture
cad.opening: Coordinates with pipe and cable outlets

objects.name: steel-frame electrical backing plate
objects.definition: A small plate or bracket fixed to steel framing to support a switch, socket, control or electrical mounting box at its required wall position.
functions: Support electrical accessories
Provide a stable mounting face
Position the accessory relative to the wall lining

cad.pattern: One at each scheduled electrical accessory
cad.placement: Fixed to a stud or between studs behind lining
cad.opening: Aligns with the lining cut-out and electrical box

objects.name: steel bottom-plate separation membrane
objects.definition: An impermeable strip placed between an external perimeter steel bottom track and a concrete slab or other moisture-retaining support to separate the coated frame from dampness.
functions: Separate the steel track from ground or slab moisture
Reduce moisture contact at the weather-side flange
Maintain a compatible interface between frame and support

cad.pattern: Continuous strip under applicable perimeter bottom tracks
cad.placement: Between steel bottom track and slab or moisture-retaining support
cad.opening: Perforated only at anchors and services while maintaining separation

notes: The cited BlueScope requirement is product and warranty guidance; it is not restated as a universal NCC mandate.

objects.name: steel-frame isolation membrane
objects.definition: A compatible separating layer inserted where coated steel framing would otherwise contact a moisture-retaining or chemically incompatible material.
functions: Prevent incompatible direct material contact
Interrupt moisture wicking to the steel frame
Protect the metallic coating at interfaces

cad.pattern: Local or continuous layer at incompatible interfaces
cad.placement: Between coated steel and the incompatible or moisture-retaining material
cad.opening: Detailed around fixings without creating an unintended moisture bridge

objects.name: steel framing self-drilling screw
objects.definition: A screw with a drill-shaped point and thread suited to forming its own hole and fastening thin steel framing members or compatible attached components.
functions: Connect steel framing parts
Attach brackets, battens, sheets or accessories
Form a repeatable mechanical frame connection

cad.pattern: Repeated at every scheduled screw connection
cad.placement: Through connected sheets or sections

notes: Tek is retained as a proprietary search term, not the canonical name.

objects.name: steel framing rivet
objects.definition: A permanent mechanical fastener inserted through aligned holes and deformed to clamp cold-formed steel framing parts together.
functions: Join thin steel components
Clamp overlapping frame parts
Provide a factory or site connection where the system specifies riveting
materials: aluminium rivet where compatible and specified

cad.pattern: At each scheduled riveted connection
cad.placement: Through overlapping framing components

objects.name: steel framing clinch joint
objects.definition: A formed connection made by locally punching and interlocking overlapping thin steel sheets without adding a separate screw or rivet.
functions: Join overlapping cold-formed steel parts
Create a repeatable factory connection
Hold frame components without a separate loose fastener

cad.pattern: At factory-defined frame intersections
cad.placement: In overlapping thin steel sheets

notes: The joint is a permanent deformation of the connected parts, not a separate loose fastener object.

objects.name: steel-frame masonry anchor
objects.definition: An expansion, screw or other approved anchor used to fix a cold-formed steel frame component to concrete or masonry support.
functions: Fasten frame to concrete or masonry
Transfer scheduled shear or tension
Locate the frame during erection and service

cad.pattern: At scheduled frame-to-masonry or frame-to-concrete locations
cad.placement: Through frame plate or bracket into substrate
cad.load: Frame anchorage to concrete or masonry

notes: Dynabolt is retained only as a proprietary search term.
